main_text.p: rio inscribebant. Mercurius præest sapientiæ & eloquio. Pythagoras,Plato, Democritus, Eudoxus, & multi sa- cerdotes Ægyptios accesserunt. Hactenus Jamblichus.Neq; contraria vitæ instituta vel genera Mercurium hunc sectatum fuisse quispiam opinetur,quòd Philosophus fuit, & leges simul condidit. Cicero enim de legibus ait:Non à prætoris edicto,ut pleriq̄ nunc; neque à XII. tabulis,ut superiores: sed penitus ex intima philosophia hauriendam juris disciplinam puto. Et Hegendorphinus in Epitome sua Juris civilis, philosophos theses tradere dicit, Jureconsultos hypotheses.Id quod multis ibidem exemplis declarat.

Solon deinde Salaminius, circa annum mundi 3380 claruit, septem Græciæ sapientum sapientissimus, uti Plato in Timæo ipsum vocat.Hujus temporibus cùm magna in aristocratica Atheniensium rep. dissensio esset,& optimates ab infima plebe ita dissilirent,ut nulla ratione æquari, aut imperiis & honoribus exæquari inter se, & cum repub. conciliari posse videretur; Solon hoc se effecturum, ac, si legum ferendarum jus haberet, leges potentibus & tenuibus,patritiis & plebeiis æquales laturum pollicebatur. Unde factum, ut Solonem utrique amplexi, legibus ferendis, ac reip. Atheniensium constituendæ præficerent. Et, ut Plutarchus in vita Solonis author est, communi jurejurando senatus se adstringit, Solonis leges ratas habiturum, privatim etiam unusquisque prætorum in foro ad lapidem addito juramento, se, si quid contra eas constitutiones committat, aurem statuam, pondere se Solon Salaminius.

page.notes: Right-hand strip of the neighbouring page: cut off and illegible, not transcribed. Running head as printed reads "LIBRI I." with "Iuris" at the far right corner; the word "Iuris" is not included in running_head and may be the right-hand running head. Left-margin marks (small brackets and strokes) are not text and are omitted. Possible printing error: "aurem" (probably intended as aureum), left as printed. "Pythagoras,Plato," and the following line are set in italic, but the italic extent is uncertain there. Long s has been written as s throughout.
